title: Derived limit of an inverse system
statement:
Let $\mathcal D$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] (with shift $[1]$ and its class of distinguished triangles), and let $(K_n,f_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse system of objects of $\mathcal D$ [def-weil-inverse-system], with transition maps $f_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n$. Assume that the product $\prod_{n\geq1}K_n$, with projections $\mathrm{pr}_n$, exists in $\mathcal D$ [def-weil-category-product] (it does when $\mathcal D$ has countable products), and let $1-s:\prod_nK_n\to\prod_nK_n$ be the transition endomorphism of the system [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism], the morphism with $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ(1-s)=\mathrm{pr}_n-f_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$, i.e. $(k_n)_n\mapsto(k_n-f_n(k_{n+1}))_n$.

A *derived limit* (or *homotopy limit*) of $(K_n,f_n)$ is a triple $(K,p,\delta)$ of an object $K$ of $\mathcal D$ and morphisms $p:K\to\prod_nK_n$, $\delta:\prod_nK_n\to K[1]$ such that

$$
 K\xrightarrow{\ p\ }\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{\ 1-s\ }\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }K[1]
$$

is a distinguished triangle; this triangle is the *Roos triangle* of the derived limit. An object $K$ *is a derived limit* of the system if there exist $p,\delta$ making $(K,p,\delta)$ a derived limit, and one then writes $K=R\varprojlim_nK_n$.

What is defined is thus a property of an object together with a triangle, not an object attached to the system and not a functor: the notation $R\varprojlim_nK_n$ denotes any such $K$, and no choice is made. That a derived limit exists whenever $\prod_nK_n$ exists, and that any two are isomorphic though not canonically, are claims, not part of the definition; so is the existence of a (non-unique) morphism of derived limits compatible with the Roos triangles for a morphism of inverse systems. No resolution of the system is chosen and no model of $\mathcal D$ is fixed. (Sign convention: Bhatt-Scholze use $t-\mathrm{id}=-(1-s)$; a triangle $K\xrightarrow{p}\prod K_n\xrightarrow{-(1-s)}\prod K_n\xrightarrow{\delta}K[1]$ is distinguished if and only if $K\xrightarrow{p}\prod K_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod K_n\xrightarrow{-\delta}K[1]$ is, being isomorphic to it by $(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id},-\mathrm{id})$, so both conventions give the same objects $K$.)

This is Definition Tag [08TC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08TC) of the Stacks Project, Section Derived limits (Tag 08TB).

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks derived.tex Tag 08TC (line 10442) with its following paragraph and Remark 0H9J, more-algebra.tex Tag 0CQD, and Bhatt-Scholze Prop. 3.1.10/3.1.11 (p. 17). Corrected the formula of 1-s: the node had $f_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n$ but wrote $k_n-f_{n+1}(k_{n+1})$ (Stacks' indexing), which does not type-check; it is now $k_n-f_n(k_{n+1})$. Made the defined datum precise: a derived limit is a triple $(K,p,\delta)$ whose Roos triangle is distinguished (the old text left $p$, $\delta$ implicit), and stated explicitly that existence, uniqueness up to non-unique isomorphism and morphisms for maps of systems are claims, not part of the definition, with pointers to lem-weil-derived-limit-existence (clause 1), the new lem-weil-derived-limit-morphism (Stacks 0H9J), lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso, prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality and lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit; added the Bhatt-Scholze sign convention remark.
